After clearing, Metacat can no longer "remember" previous answers or get "reminded" of similar problems. Each subsequent run starts fresh, without bias from prior solutions.

Episodic memory is the one thing that carries from one run to the next, so clearing it is what separates one training session from the next. Everything else -- the slipnet, the themespace, the workspace, the trace -- is rebuilt for every run anyway.
Does NOT affect the current run, run history, or any engine configuration (slipnet nodes, codelet types, parameters, etc.).
Useful when you want the system to approach a problem without influence from answers it found before, or when past entries are no longer relevant.
technical_description: Calls DELETE /api/memory, which deletes every row from the answer_descriptions and snag_descriptions tables and clears the process-wide EpisodicMemory object in place, so live runners holding a reference see the change.
Both halves are necessary: the Memory panel reads the rows, so clearing only the in-process object left every answer still on screen and looked like the clear had not worked.
Does NOT touch the runs, run_state_captures, audit_actions or trace_events tables. Run history and everything the persistence modes recorded survive.
Bumps the store epoch counter so the Memory panel re-renders even if the data shape is unchanged.
Episodic Memory will begin accumulating new entries on subsequent runs as answers and snags are discovered.

title: Full Reset (delete everything)
short_desc: Completely resets Petacat -- deletes all runs, clears memory, and returns the UI to its initial state.

user_description: Completely resets Petacat to its initial state, as if you had just opened it for the first time.
Stops any currently running engine execution.
Deletes EVERY run ever created, together with their trace events.
Clears all episodic memory (answer and snag descriptions).
Resets all UI panels to their empty/default state.
This is the "start completely over" button. Use it when you want a clean slate with no leftover data from previous sessions.
technical_description: Calls DELETE /api/runs, which deletes all rows from the runs, trace_events, answer_descriptions, snag_descriptions and (legacy, no longer written) cycle_snapshots tables.
It does NOT currently delete the run_state_captures, audit_actions or training_sessions rows that Normal and Audit runs wrote, so those are left behind without the runs they belong to.
Calls DELETE /api/memory to clear the in-memory episodic memory store.
Resets all Zustand store state: runId, workspace, slipnet, coderack, themespace, trace, memory, temperature, commentary, and codeletCount.
Bumps the store epoch to force all components to re-fetch and re-render.
Sets the internal _stopRequested flag to halt any in-progress run loop.
Database seed data (slipnet nodes, codelet types, engine parameters, urgency levels, formula coefficients, demo problems, etc.) is NOT affected. Only user-created run data is deleted.

title: Regenerate Help Documentation
short_desc: Re-syncs help text from the JSON source of truth into the database and regenerates derived artifacts.

user_description: Re-reads the help text source file (seed_data/help_topics.en.json or the current locale file) and re-applies it everywhere the help system uses it.
The ? popovers in every dashboard panel immediately reflect any edits you've made to the JSON -- no backend restart required.
Also refreshes the static reference file HELP.md and the developer TypeScript key constants. This is useful in development when iterating on help wording.
Safe to run at any time. It is not destructive and doesn't affect runs, memory, or any other state.

In production deployments (where the frontend is pre-bundled) the popovers still update from the database, but the TypeScript constants file is a dev-only artifact and requires a rebuild to take effect in the compiled bundle.
technical_description: Calls POST /api/admin/help/regenerate, which runs two steps on the backend.

Step 1 -- DB sync: invokes server.main._sync_help_topics(), which reads seed_data/help_topics.{locale}.json and performs an idempotent UPSERT into the help_topics table keyed by topic_key. Existing rows are updated, new rows are inserted. No deletes.

Step 2 -- file regeneration: calls server.services.help_docs.regenerate_all(), which rewrites HELP.md and client/src/constants/helpTopics.ts from the same JSON. Writes are skipped if the content already matches on disk, so the operation is a no-op when nothing has changed.

The same sync runs automatically every time the backend starts (from server/main.py lifespan), and the CLI script scripts/generate_help_docs.py is a thin wrapper around the same functions for use from a terminal or CI job.
Tests in tests/integration/test_help_topics.py and tests/e2e/test_help_api.py validate the JSON schema, drift between the JSON and generated files, and that every panel's help topic is fetchable.

title: Run Parameters
short_desc: The twenty-seven engine settings that are fixed before a run starts and cannot change while it thinks.
full_desc:
Twenty-seven entries in the engine's parameter set are read while it thinks: thresholds that decide what reaches the Temporal Trace, the periods governing clamps and settling, the Coderack's capacity and urgency resolution, the Themespace's boost, decay and spread, and the update cadence.

Each can be set for one run. Omitted parameters keep the global default, and an unknown name or an out-of-range value is refused rather than ignored — ignoring a typo would give you a run at the default while the record said otherwise. Because they are fixed at creation, changing one starts a new run rather than altering the loaded one.

The whole resolved set is stored with a Normal or Audit run, not just what you changed. That is deliberate: if only your overrides were kept, reading them later would mean reading them against whatever the defaults had become, and the run's record would quietly change meaning.

Not every engine setting is offered. Display timings and a handful the port reads nowhere are excluded, because a control that changes nothing is worse than no control. Three parameters that name Slipnet nodes are shown read-only: a wrong node name is not a typo a run recovers from.

Distinct from the derived values shown beside them, which are outputs rather than settings — which numeric backend ran, how the Coderack sharded, the config and memory hashes.
